Fit a time-to-event model

Source: R/survkit.R
survkit.Rd

One interface over the established survival stack. method selects an estimator from the registry (survkit_methods()); the appropriate backend is checked, a small-sample power gate runs (survkit_power()), and the fit is returned as a single typed object (survkit_fit) with consistent print, summary, coef, vcov, predict and tidy() methods.

Usage

survkit(
  formula,
  data,
  method = "weibull",
  ...,
  check_power = TRUE,
  warn_underpowered = TRUE,
  on_underpowered = c("warn", "abstain")
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula, e.g. survival::Surv(time, status) ~ x.

data

A data frame.

method

Character registry key (default "weibull"); see survkit_methods().

...

Passed to the backend estimator.

check_power

Logical; run the events-per-variable gate (default TRUE).

warn_underpowered

Logical; warn when the gate flags the model under-powered (default TRUE). Ignored when on_underpowered = "abstain".

on_underpowered

One of "warn" (default) or "abstain". "warn" preserves the historical behaviour: the model is fitted regardless, with a warning when warn_underpowered is TRUE. "abstain" declines to fit at all when the gate flags the model under-powered, returning a survkit_refusal() instead – the typed token an orchestra-level caller can recognise via is_orchestra_decline().

Value

A survkit_fit object, or a survkit_refusal() when on_underpowered = "abstain" and the power gate is not satisfied.

Details

The left-hand side of formula is a survival::Surv() response. Extra arguments in ... pass straight to the backend estimator, so any backend option remains reachable.

See also

survkit_methods() for the registry, survkit_power() for the gate.

Other model-fitting: is_survkit_refusal(), survkit_cuminc(), survkit_power(), survkit_refusal(), survkit_rmst(), survkit_score(), survkit_triangulate()

Examples

df <- survival::lung
fit <- survkit(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex, df, method = "weibull")
fit
#> <survkit_fit> method = weibull (parametric, via flexsurv)
#>   n = 228   events = 165
#>   power: ok (82.5 events/predictor)
#>   coefficients:
#>   shape   scale     age     sex 
#>  0.2823  6.2749 -0.0123  0.3821 
coef(fit)
#>       shape       scale         age         sex 
#>  0.28229534  6.27485306 -0.01225703  0.38208514
